questions.question: Define mass communication. How does it differ from interpersonal and group communication?
questions.solution_html:
• Mass communication targets large, dispersed audiences through mass media, without
  • direct sender-receiver interaction- deliver a single message to millions simultaneously.
  • Interpersonal communication - direct, person-to-person contact using spoken words,
  • facial expressions, gestures, postures, and tone of voice. Group communication expands
  • this to more than two people, allowing exchange of ideas, experiences, and information,
  • supporting collective decision-making. [U/CO1]

questions.question: Critically evaluate the different theories of media influence discussed in the passage. Which theory do you find most relevant in today’s digital media environment, and why?
questions.solution_html:
• 1. The Medium, Not the Message (Marshall McLuhan) electronic media exert a
  • profound influence on human behaviour, not through the messages they convey, but
  • through the sensory environment they create. 2. Reinforcement Theory (Joseph
  • Klapper) mass media primarily reinforces existing beliefs, values and social norms rather
  • than introducing significant change. 3. Narcotising Dysfunction (Lazarsfeld and
  • Merton) Exposure to a constant stream of information result in superficial awareness
  • without corresponding engagement.4. Catharsis Theory (Seymour Feshbach) media
  • serve as a psychological outlet, allowing individuals to purge aggressive/ antisocial
  • emotions through vicarious experiences. 5. Media as Windows on the World (Edward
  • Shils and David M White) democratise access to cultural content by making more of the
  • good accessible to more people. 6. Corruptive Effects (Fredric Wertham) media content
  • fosters materialism, antisocial behaviour and emotional desensitisation causing damage
  • to moral and social development. [U/CO1]

questions.question: Analyse the different types of news.
questions.solution_html:
• Types of news 1.Direct/Straight news is a straight forward account of a happening. It
  • usually answers five Ws (what, when, where, who, why) and one H (how). These five
  • Ws and one H are known as news elements. Three key parts of a news story are the
  • headline, the lead and remainder. 2. Feature - It goes beyond a direct news story. It
  • explores the background, probes in depth an idea or event. [U/CO2]
